4.4	Training

The Scottsboro Water, Sewer, & Gas Board Wastewater Treatment Plant trains personnel in the operating procedures to help ensure safe and effective performance of their assigned tasks. A record of all training is maintained to help ensure new and refresher training is provided on a timely basis.

4.5	Maintenance

The Scottsboro Water, Sewer, & Gas Board Wastewater Treatment Plant properly maintains the equipment in our processes.  The Scottsboro Water, Sewer, & Gas Board Wastewater Treatment Plant maintenance program includes:

1. procedures to safely guide workers in their maintenance tasks,
2. worker training in the maintenance procedures, and
3. inspection and testing program to help identify equipment deterioration and damage before equipment fails.

4.6	Compliance Audits

The Scottsboro Water, Sewer, & Gas Board Wastewater Treatment Plant performs periodic (at least every three years) audits of covered processes to verify the processes are operating in compliance with the requirements of the RMP Rule.  A compliance audit report is prepared after each audit, and any deficiencies noted by the audit are corrected in a timely manner.

4.7	Incident Investigations

The Scottsboro Water, Sewer, & Gas Board Wastewater Treatment Plant investigates all incidents that could reasonably have resulted in a serious injury to personnel, the public, or the environment.  The Scottsboro Water, Sewer, & Gas Board Wastewater Treatment Plant trains employees to identify and report any and all incidents requiring investigation.  An investigation team is assembled and the investigation is initiated within 48 hours of the incident.  The results of the investigation are documented, recommendations are resolved, and appropriate process enhancements are implemented.

RISK MANAGEMENT PROGRAM
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY


1.0	Accidental Release Prevention and Emergency Response Policies

The Scottsboro Water, Sewer, & Gas Board Wastewater Treatment Plant is committed to the safety of our workers, the public, and the environment.  The resources invested in the prevention of accidental releases of hazardous substances demonstrate this commitment.  The Scottsboro Water, Sewer, & Gas Board Wastewater Treatment Plant implements reasonable controls, such as training of personnel and the safe design, installation, operation and maintenance of our processes.  Our policy is to make every effort to prevent the release of hazardous substances but in the event of a release, our trained personnel and local emergency response agencies will respond to control and contain the release in a manner that will be safe for workers and will help prevent injuries to the public or the environment.


2.0	Description of The Scottsboro Water, Sewer, & Gas Board Wastewater Treatment Plant and Regulated Substances

The Scottsboro Water, Sewer, & Gas Board Wastewater Treatment Plant handles one substance regulated by the Risk Management Plan Rule (RMP Rule) in quantities above the Threshold Quantity.  This substance is:

* Chlorine - stored in 1 ton cylinders and used for disinfection of the treated water prior to release to the receiving stream.


3.0	Hazard Assessment
 
The RMP Rule requires The Scottsboro Water, Sewer, & Gas Board Wastewater Treatment Plant to perform a Hazard Assessment of the regulated substances stored and used in the covered processes at the facility.  This Hazard Assessment includes an offsite consequence analysis for the following scenarios:
 
* One worst-case and one alternative release scenario for the toxic substance chlorine for the chlorination process unit at the facility.

The Scottsboro Water, Sewer, & Gas Board Wastewater Treatment Plant completed a Hazard Assessment for th

e covered processes and the results have been appropriately communicated to the local emergency response agencies. The Hazard Assessment has been recently updated to reflect changes in population.


4.0	Accidental Release Prevention Program and Chemical-Specific Prevention Steps

The RMP Rule requires that a prevention program be established for The Scottsboro Water, Sewer, & Gas Board Wastewater Treatment Plant chlorination processes.  The following details the prevention program elements at The Scottsboro Water, Sewer, & Gas Board Wastewater Treatment Plant that apply to these processes.

4.1	Safety Information

The Scottsboro Water, Sewer, & Gas Board Wastewater Treatment Plant maintains a variety of technical documents that are used to help ensure safe operation of The Scottsboro Water, Sewer, & Gas Board Wastewater Treatment Plant processes.  Safety data sheets (SDSs) document the physical and chemical properties of hazardous substances handled at The Scottsboro Water, Sewer, & Gas Board Wastewater Treatment Plant, including the chlorine in the covered process.  The engineering design documents include the operating parameters, the design basis and configuration of the equipment in each covered process, and references to applicable codes and standards.

4.2	Hazard Review

The Scottsboro Water, Sewer, & Gas Board Wastewater Treatment Plant performs and periodically updates hazard reviews of the covered processes to help identify and control process hazards.  Checklists are used to guide the hazard review.  These checklists include items to help ensure The Scottsboro Water, Sewer, & Gas Board Wastewater Treatment Plant operates and maintains the equipment in a manner consistent with the applicable design specifications, codes, standards, and regulations.

4.3	Operating Procedures

The Scottsboro Water, Sewer, & Gas Board Wastewater Treatment Plant develops and maintains operating procedures to define how tasks related to process operations should be performed.  T

c Prevention Steps - Chlorine

Industry standards are followed at The Scottsboro Water, Sewer, & Gas Board Wastewater Treatment Plant to help ensure safe handling of chlorine.  The vendor supplies chlorine via a Department of Transportation (DOT) approved truck and in DOT approved 1 ton cylinders.  The process equipment is designed and constructed with state-of-the-art materials and technology utilizing the standards and guidelines of the Chlorine Institute, American Water Works Association, ASME, ANSI, and other applicable codes.  Workers who perform operations involving chlorine receive training emphasizing safe handling procedures according to the guidelines required by The Scottsboro Water, Sewer, & Gas Board Wastewater Treatment Plant.


5.0	Five Year Accident History

5.1 Description of the Incident in Chronological Order

During a routine Chlorine Cylinder Change out at the Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) at approximately 12:15pm on Friday October 4th, 2024, two operators were attempting to change a Chlorine Gas (Cl2) cylinder. During the change of the Cl2 cylinder, both employees observed a routine gas leak around the threads of the valve and immediately shut the valve to the cylinder. The affected employee recognized he inhaled chlorine gas due to an equipment failure that occurred from one of the canisters not being installed and tightened properly on his mask. Both employees immediately exited the Chlorine Room, in order not to be further exposed to Chlorine Gas vapors, and to get fresh air.  Once outside the Chlorine Room, the affected employee removed his mask and tightened the loose cylinder. Both employees took a short break to ensure adequate fresh air was received prior to continuing.  At this time, the employee did not feel any effects from the Chlorine gas. The affected employee verified to his coworker that he was capable of completing the task of Cl2 cylinder change, so both employees put their masks back on and then re-entered the Chlorine Ro

om to complete the change of the cylinder.

The affected employee left work for the day however after arriving home, he realized he might need to get checked out by a medical professional after feeling shortness of breath and chest tightness.
 
At 3:15 PM on 10/4/2024 the WWTP Superintendent called our Employee Injury Triage number per protocol. Triage advised the Employee to seek medical attention at Highlands Medical Center ER. Superintendent and affected employee were already in route to the ER during the call.

Once at Highlands Medical Center ER the employee was evaluated, and it was suggested the employee follow up with Primary Physician or Scottsboro Urgent Care in 2-3 days with a return-to-work date of October 7th, 2025. 

5.2 Emergency Response/ Hazmat Actions Taken

No Emergency Response/Hazmat Actions were required. 

5.3 Contributing Factors

Contributing Factors- Human Error

Human Error was a Contributing Factor in this incident due to the fact the employee did not properly inspect his mask cartridges before entering the Chlorine Room to change a Cylinder. 

5.4 Findings

Due to the nature of the injury occurring from an Equipment Failure on a mask, due to Human Error, Scottsboro WWTP has now implemented an additional equipment check list to include the inspection of PPE to include checking for properly tightened canisters on masks prior to entering the Chlorine Room and prior to performing work on a Chlorine Cylinder. 


6.0	Emergency Response 

The Scottsboro Water, Sewer, & Gas Board Wastewater Treatment Plant has prepared a written emergency response/action plan that complies with the RMP Rule, other federal standards and industry guidelines.  This plan has been communicated to the Local Emergency Planning Committee LEPC/EMA and local fire department under the coordination rules of the RMP.


7.0	Planned Changes to Improve Safety

The Scottsboro Water, Sewer, & Gas Board Wastewater Treatment Plant continuously attempts to improve the safety of our

processes to protect our employees, the public and the environment.  The Scottsboro Water, Sewer, & Gas Board Wastewater Treatment Plant incident investigations, employee suggestions and improvements in technology are utilized to update the safety aspects of the processes.
